bc_dysphorium.blurb: Dysphorium sits at the far left end of The Fortress at Skaha Bluffs in the Okanagan. It has seven routes, mostly sport with a pair of trad lines, and nearly all of them fall in the 5.11 range with a single 5.10. The climbing is moderate in character, with short, pumpy lines toward the left side. The cliff gets sun in the morning, roughly from eight until early afternoon in high season. It sees less traffic than the other sections of The Fortress.

bc_big_tree.blurb: Big Tree is a section of The Fortress at Skaha Bluffs in the Okanagan, named for a huge Douglas fir that marks the spot along the main trail. It holds seven routes: mostly trad, plus a couple of sport lines. Most grades land in the 5.10 range with two 5.11s. The routes here tend to be long, and a few are mixed or run to two pitches, which makes it a good stop for climbers wanting longer leads at a moderate grade.

bc_swiss_cheese.blurb: Swiss Cheese is a small wall at Nordic Rock in Whistler, and it is the first wall you meet on the Nordic approach, a short walk up through talus and into the trees. Seven routes, six of them sport and one trad, mostly easy to moderate from 5.7 to 5.10, with a single much harder 5.13 line. Several of the easier climbs follow pockets, which makes the wall a friendly choice for newer climbers or a relaxed outing.

bc_preview_wall.blurb: Preview Wall is a sport wall at Area 44 in the Sea to Sky region. It is the second cluster of routes you reach on the trail in, just beyond the first wall. Seven sport routes run from 5.6 up to 5.10, with most in the 5.9 to 5.10 range and a couple of easier ones at the bottom. It is known as a good concentration of moderates. A helmet is advised here, as at the rest of Area 44.

bc_marbles_wall.blurb: Marbles Wall is a sport wall within Area 44 in the Sea to Sky region. The terrain runs from slabby to vertical. Its seven routes span 5.8 to 5.11, with four of them at 5.10 and just one at the top end. The wall picks up sun in the afternoon, dries quickly, and gives good views even from the base of some climbs.
